authored_from: mixed — see provenance; batch 1 from secondary sources, batch 2 with the corpus visible under a measured containment guard
notes: corpus_law is a substring matched against law_name in data/processed/articles.jsonl; law_name comes from the mandatory --law flag on ingest.
Scoring is refused when the ingested corpus is a different law: 151/2020 questions run against قانون المرافعات would look like bad retrieval, not like a mismatched eval set.
corpus_law_status must become CONFIRMED (the official PDF is in data/raw/ and ingested) before any number is published.

overlap_band caps AND floors how much of a question's wording is shared with the article that answers it (ADR-009). Too high = BM25 wins for free. Too low in a `direct` question = BM25 has nothing to match and the lexical baseline is unfairly crushed; that belongs in the `colloquial` category, which is where paraphrase robustness is tested on purpose.

split=test is held out: load_questions() returns dev unless a caller names the split, so the test rows stay unrun. They exist to check later whether a configuration chosen on dev survives questions that never informed it — an answer worth nothing once they have been scored against. verify-refs is the one caller that reads both, because it validates article references against the corpus text and touches no retrieval output.

batch_1.authored_from: secondary web sources (paraphrased); all 20 article references machine-verified against the ingested corpus on 2026-09-08

batch_2.authored_from: written against the ingested corpus with the article text visible, 2026-09-23
batch_2.why_this_is_weaker: A question written while looking at its own answer tends to reuse the answer's wording, which hands BM25 a match it did not earn and inflates every lexical baseline it appears in.
batch_2.mitigation: The containment band is measured, not asserted: 22 of the first 40 drafts were rejected by it (19 above band, 3 below) and rewritten before anything was committed. Six further drafts were dropped for redundant article coverage. verify-refs re-checks every surviving row at scoring time, so a leaky question cannot reach a number.
